analytical_question: Can both shifts operate a four-week shadow pilot now, and can the retailer sustain routine use?
general_et_finding: An item tag can identify an individual garment during a count; the GS1 case establishes deployment precedent, not local accuracy.
application_finding: Comparing a shadow count of denim with manual recounts can expose stock discrepancies. A tag read alone cannot establish which stock record needs correction.
organization_specific_finding: Sponsorship supported: four-week sponsor commitment. Skills supported for counting: two leads passed exercise. Workflow gap: no closing investigator or accepted handoff. Infrastructure/data supported for scope: reader, verified tag mapping and barcode fallback. Resources mixed: pilot hours funded; no recurring budget. Governance supported for corrections: controller approval and no scan writeback. Culture/change partially supported: one reported mismatch without penalty, too little to infer store-wide trust. Operating ownership gap: the count lead and deputy collect reads but nobody owns off-duty discrepancies.

evidence.claim: I.T.’S. international used individually tagged garments for inventory counts in apparel stores.
evidence.date_or_recency: GS1 Japan case study, 2012; reviewed November 8, 2026.
evidence.notes: Establishes precedent; no transfer of time savings or present staffing readiness.

evidence.claim: Sponsor funds four weeks of one-store shadow counts. Two shift leads passed a count exercise; staff logged a mismatch without penalty. Stockroom has a reader, verified tag-to-SKU list and barcode recount procedure. Inventory Controller approves ledger corrections after recount; scans cannot write to the ledger. One named floor lead plus a trained deputy can collect counts. Both shifts have reserved count time. The closing shift has no designated discrepancy investigator when the controller is off duty. Nobody has accepted that shift handoff. No ongoing budget beyond week four.
evidence.notes: Accepted for the exercise; not audited employer records.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Training and protected count time support a trial but do not establish sustained ownership. The case does not establish value or routine readiness.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the scoped judgment given the case facts; actual execution is unverified.
value_opportunity_implication: Count fully reconciled size/color discrepancies and total staff time, including exception work. Fast scanning alone cannot show operational value.
risk_governance_implication: Keep scans read-only. Escalate unresolved records rather than silently adjusting stock; controller retains correction authority.
recommendation_management_implication: Hold both-shift pilot. First, retail operations sponsor should assign the closing queue and backup, reserve recount time and obtain acceptance. Second, store lead should stage a missing-tag case with the controller absent: log, recount, escalate and leave stock unchanged until approved. Third, sponsor must fund recurring coverage before routine use. A staffed daytime read-only rehearsal can test tag capture now. It cannot test closing reconciliation. Waiting until morning is acceptable only under an agreed handoff with a named recipient, which this profile lacks.
change_monitoring_triggers: Do not authorize both shifts until a signed roster and passed handoff drill exist.
At week four review unresolved cases by shift, recount labor and recurring ownership; send value and adoption tradeoffs to the Adoption Agent.

Proposed week-four rule: sponsor may consider routine use only with a complete exception log, every discrepancy accepted by a named owner or explicitly escalated by shift close, no overdue unresolved cases, zero unauthorized ledger corrections, and a funded roster whose reserved hours cover measured work. Missing logs: withhold. A missed handoff: hold, repair and retest. An unauthorized correction: stop immediately and investigate.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Ask the sponsor who can fund and own recurring work beyond week four.
